signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry + Options Skew + Retail Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 163.77, maintaining a robust profile above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following the end of Gulf War hostilities. A +275bp USD carry advantage (SOFR 3.64% vs TONA 0.98%) remains the structural anchor, while the VIX at 18.7 (normal volatility) fails to trigger safe-haven JPY demand. Despite the price strength, the 25d Risk Reversal at -1.54 reveals a strong put skew, indicating institutional desks are paying a premium for downside protection against potential BoJ intervention. Retail sentiment has reached an extreme 86% short, directly diverging from the COT LF net short of -114,030, suggesting retail is fading the move while institutions remain short JPY. This setup creates a high-conviction carry environment with tail-risk protection being actively sought via options. Risk: BoJ delivers a hawkish surprise at the July 31 meeting, compressing the 266bp OIS differential.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT vs CB Divergence + Inflation Risk
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6992, holding above its SMA20 (0.6957) as markets position for high-impact Australian CPI data. RBA holds at 4.35%. This positioning aligns with a -71bp carry advantage for the AUD (AONIA 4.35% vs SOFR 3.64%), making AUD a preferred G10 carry destination. However, the AUD 25d Risk Reversal at -0.86 shows a moderate put skew, suggesting the options market is hedging against a potential CPI miss that would invalidate the RBA's hiking bias. Price remains contained below the SMA50 at 0.7027, which serves as the primary technical ceiling ahead of Governor Bullock's upcoming speech. Risk: Australian CPI misses expectations, forcing a rapid unwind of the speculative net long.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Real Rate Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5770 continues to trade near its monthly lows despite a hawkish RBNZ policy bias and a cycle of data outperformance (ESI +22.2). COT LF positioning has reached a bearish extreme with net short -31,649 (only 12.0% long), while the RBNZ real rate of -1.56% remains the most accommodative in the G10. This negative real rate explains the speculative appetite for shorts despite the nominal 2.5% rate. The pair is currently testing support just above the SMA20 (0.5759), with the +125bp USD carry advantage (SOFR 3.64% vs OCR 2.50%) providing a persistent headwind for the Kiwi. The combination of extreme speculative shorting and positive economic surprises creates an asymmetric setup for a squeeze if RBNZ rhetoric hardens. Risk: RBNZ signals a shift away from its hiking bias, validating the extreme spec short.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Premium + ESI Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD at 1.1377 remains pressured below its SMA20/50/200 cluster, reflecting a moderate negative bias in the Economic Surprise Index (ESI -12.6). The +145bp carry spread (SOFR 3.64% vs ESTR 2.19%) favors the USD, which is supported by a restrictive +1.47% real rate compared to the EUR's +0.16%. Options markets are pricing an elevated vol risk premium (VRP) of +2.5%, with IV at 7.1% vs HV30 at 4.5%, suggesting heightened demand for protection ahead of the July 29 FOMC meeting. COT LF net shorts at -80,570 confirm that institutional positioning is already aligned with the fundamental downside, leaving the pair vulnerable to a consolidation phase rather than a fresh breakdown. A sustained close above the SMA20 at 1.1419 is required to shift the immediate bearish technical bias. Risk: FOMC delivers a dovish hold, triggering a short-covering rally toward 1.1500.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Correlation Break + Carry Advantage
signals.text: USD/CAD is trading at 1.4120, currently exhibiting a significant correlation break against WTI Oil (corr -0.916 vs norm +0.022, z = -1.56σ). While WTI is down -0.84% session-to-date at $81.9, the CAD is failing to track oil price action, instead being driven by the +150bp USD carry advantage (Fed 3.75% vs BoC 2.25%). COT LF positioning remains heavily net short CAD (-99,823, 18.8% long), indicating a crowded trade that has successfully faded recent CAD strength. Price is currently holding below the SMA20 (1.4131) but remains well above the SMA200 (1.3849), confirming the long-term bullish trend for the pair. The divergence from oil suggest that the interest rate differential is the primary driver in the current regime. Risk: A sharp reversal in oil prices above $85/bbl forces a CAD short-covering event.
